distractors.reason: 'Heavily' describes weight, force or a large amount, as in 'rain heavily'. We don't use it to describe how someone reads.
'Strictly' describes following rules or limits, as in 'strictly forbidden'. It does not describe the way you read a report.
'Sharply' describes a sudden change or a clear, quick movement. We don't say 'read sharply' to mean paying close attention.

example_sentence: Please read the report ___ before the meeting.
l1_interference: Polscy użytkownicy języka angielskiego często stawiają przysłówek przed czasownikiem, mówiąc 'carefully read'. Po angielsku przysłówek sposobu zwykle stoi po czasowniku: 'read carefully'.
explanation: In English, adverbs of manner usually come after the verb. 'Carefully' describes how the reading is done, so it follows 'read'.

related_collocations.example: Please listen carefully to the instructions.
She works hard on every article she writes.
I could not sleep well after reading the bad news.

memory_tip: Manner adverbs usually come AFTER the verb: read carefully, work hard, sleep well
